Petitioners have filed Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri. Yesuraj in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 19.05.2024 at about 10.30 p.m., Yesuraj was proceeding by riding two wheeler bearing No. KA.50.EJ.9951 from Sahakaranagar D block towards Kodigehalli main road, when he reached at 16th E cross road, Sahakaranagar, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Mahendra XUV 300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 came from 8 th main road towards Sahakaranagar, driven the same with high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler in which Yesuraj was proceeding and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, Yesuraj fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Bengaluru wherein the injured took treatment as an inpatient and also underwent surgery.

Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 20 years, he was working as a delivery man at Zepto and earning Rs30,000/- per month and contributed entire income to the welfare of the family.
The petitioners were entirely depending on the deceased.
Due to the sudden death of Yesuraj, they have lost the bread winner of the family and facing financial hardship.

The accident was occurred solely due to rash or negligent driving of Mahendra XUV300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 by its driver and in this regard Hebbal Traffic police have registered the case against the driver of above said vehicle in Cr No. 81/2024 for the offences punishable U/Sec.279 & 304(A) of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the R.C. owner and the 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the said Car.
Hence both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
With these averments petitioners prays to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, both the respondents have appeared before this tribunal through their respective counsels and filed separate written statements.

4. The written statement averments of the 1st respondent are as hereunder:
This respondent has submitted that, the offending Mahendra XUV 300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 was insured with the 2nd respondent insurance company vide policy No. 994092423740003854 and the same was in force as on the date of accident.
Further averred that, he was having valid driving license as on the date of accident.
With these averments, the 1st respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition against him.
5. The written statement averments of the 2nd respondent/Insurance company are as hereunder:
This respondent has contended that, there is 4 days delay in lodging the complaint.
Further it has denied the dependency of the petitioners on the deceased.
It has contended that there is no compliance of Sec.158(6) & 134 (c) of MV Act.
Further, it has denied the cause and manner of accident and contended that, it was head on collusion and the deceased himself contributed towards the cause of accident.

Further this respondent has denied the issuance of policy in respect of Monnappa vs Iythichanda Belliyappa Bheemaiah on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188719660/

Further contended that, the driver of the Mahendra XUV300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 was not having valid DL and also the vehicle was also not having valid FC and permit as on the date of accident and hence violated the policy conditions.
Further it has denied the age, avocation, income of the deceased and also the dependency of the petitioners on the income of the deceased.

3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom ?
4. What order or award?

13. The contention of the 2nd respondent is that, the complaint was lodged after the lapse of 4 days from the date of occurrence of accident.
In the instant case, the petitioners have produced police documents.
As per Ex.P.1, complaint was lodged before Hebbala Police Station on 22.05.2024.

14.

Now, at this juncture, it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court decided in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Ins. Co. Ltd., reported in 2018 (5) SCC 656 as held that, "Where there is a delay in lodging FIR or registering the case, the tribunal must examine whether the delay has been properly explained and whether the explanation is plausible''.

16. At this juncture it is worth to refer the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kusuma Latha Vs. Satbir reported in 2011 (3) SCC 646, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that, "the motor vehicles act is a beneficial legislation and that the claims under it must be decided on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities, not proof beyond reasonable doubt''.

17. Again it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in 2011 (4) SCC 693, between Ravi Vs. Badrinarayana and Others, wherein it is held that:
"It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot except a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim".

Further the Hon'ble Apex Court held that: "In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with the closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized Monnappa vs Iythichanda Belliyappa Bheemaiah on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188719660/
6 more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.

18. Apart from that, the Hon'ble Apex Court decided in Civil Appeal No. 8179/2022 between Rajwatii @ Rajjo and others Vs. United India Ins. Co. Ltd., and others held that:
"Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation and as such, while dealing with compensation cases, once the actual occurrence of the accident has been established,
the tribunal's role would be to award just and fare compensation''.

"The standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not district standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in Criminal Cases''.

Accordingly, there is no merits in the contention raised by respondent No.2 with regard to delay in lodging complaint.
20. Now, the important question before this Tribunal is to find whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of Mahendra XUV 300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 by its driver or not?.
In order to answer the aspect of rash or negligence, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.15 for discussion.

On careful perusal of Ex.P.15, i.e., charge sheet it discloses that, the investigating officer after thorough investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of Mahendra XUV 300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 for the offences punishable U/SEc.279 & 304A of IPC.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of Mahendra XUV 300 Car bearing No.
KA.12.MB.8750 by its driver.

21. Now, it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of CIVIL APPEAL NO.
OF 2025 (Arising out of SLP(C) No. 10351/2019) dated 25.02.2025 between Ranjeeth and another Vs. Abdul Kayam Neb and another held that, "once a charge sheet has been filed and the driver has been held negligent, no further evidence is required to prove that the bus was being negligently driven by the bus driver.

Balaji and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held at para 12 as hereunder: "
Filing of the charge sheet against the driver is also a prima-facie case to hold that, the driver of the said lorry was responsible for the accident and burden shifts on him to prove the same".
The above referred decisions are squarely applicable to the case on hand.

22. At the cost of repetition, the contents of complaint and charge sheet clearly reveals that, when the deceased was proceeding by riding two wheeler bearing No. KA.50.EJ.9951, the driver of the Mahendra XUV 300 Car bearing No. KA.12.MB.8750 drove the same in a rash or negligent manner,
dashed against the two wheeler and caused the accident.
Due to the said impact, the deceased Yesuraj sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the accidental injuries.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
23. ISSUE No.2:- This issue with respect to age and income of the deceased.
(a) Age:- According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 20 years as on the date of accident.
In the instant case, the respondent No.2 has denied the age of the deceased.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has produced Ex.P.19 i.e., the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card pertaining to deceased Yesuraj.
On careful perusal of the said document, it reveals that the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 04.06.2004.
The accident was occurred on 19.05.2024.
Therefore, age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 19 years 11 months and 15 days.

Therefore, by relying on the judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA 5353/2024 (MV-D) decided on 07th August 2025 between The Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub BMTC,
Shanthinagar, Bengaluru Vs. Smt. Jyothi and others, this tribunal considered the completed age of petitioner.

Managing Director, Motor Claims Hub BMTC,
Shanthinagar, Bengaluru Vs. Smt. Jyothi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the age of the petitioner is considered as 19 years as on the date of accident.
(b) Income of the deceased:-
According to the petitioners, the deceased was working as a delivery man at Zepto and also doing mason work and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

However,
respondent No.2 has denied the avocation and income of deceased.
In order to substantiate the exact income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in a case of Godabai and others Vs. Goudappa and another reported in 2024 SCC Online KAR 15570 (Decided in MFA No. 201022/2018 ( MV- D) on 04.06.2024) wherein the Hon'ble Division Bench of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that at para 18 is as here under: "In the absence of any evidence or proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority''.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

That apart, the Hon'ble High Court in M.F.A.
No.101144 of 2020 ( MV-I) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
" In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".

8 24.
In the instant case also, the petitioners have not produced the documents to establish the income of deceased.

As such in the absence of reliable document and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgments of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2022 is Rs.15,500/- per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 19.05.2024.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month by adopting the method given by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative.
25. ISSUE No.3:- This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are the father and mother of the deceased and petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are the younger brothers of the deceased Yesuraj.
In this case, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 have lost their son, petitioner Nos.3 & 4 have lost their elder brother.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Further, respondent No.2 has denied the dependency of the petitioners on the income of the deceased.
But in order to substantiate the same, respondent No.2 has not placed any oral or documentary evidence.

26. At this juncture, it is worth to refer the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered in M.F.A.No.102868 of 2014 (M.V.D.), between Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others, wherein the Hon'ble High Court held that, "even if the dependency is relevant criteria to claim compensation for loss of dependency, it does not mean financial dependency and the dependency includes gratuitous service dependency, physical dependency, emotional dependency and psychological dependency so on and so forth, which can never be equated in terms of the money.

entities.text: Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Gangappa Saunshi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even married sons and daughters are entitled for compensation not only on conventional heads, but also on loss of dependency".

Hence, this tribunal is of the opinion that,
Petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
In the instant case, the deceased was a bachelor, hence 1/2 of the amount is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
27. Already this Tribunal has observed that, as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 19 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".

"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
Monnappa vs Iythichanda Belliyappa Bheemaiah on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188719660/
9 28.
In this case the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 19 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling, 40% of the income of Rs.16,500/- is Rs.6,600/-.

By adding the said amount with Rs.16,500/-, monthly income of deceased would be Rs.23,100/- (i.e.,
Rs.16,500 + Rs.6,600/-).
In this case petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the deceased as a bachelor, 1/2 of the amount is to be deducted towards personal expenses of deceased.
After deducting 1/2 from Rs.23,100/- the actual monthly income would be Rs.11,500/- (i.e, Rs.23,100 - Rs.11,550).
Then, total income of the deceased per annum would be Rs.1,38,600/- (Rs.11,550/- x 12).
29. As discussed supra, the deceased was 19 years old at the time of death, the proper multiplier applicable to the age of deceased is 18.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.1,38,600/- x 18 = Rs.24,94,800/- towards for loss of dependency.

30. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

sentences.text: According to the petitioners, they have spent some amount towards funeral and obsequies ceremony expenses.

31. Now, the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the petitioner Nos.1 & 2 are the father and mother of deceased and petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are the younger brothers of deceased.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.
The Hon'ble Apex Court held that, the parents and children are having right to get the compensation under filial consortium.
Therefore, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.18,150/- is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.18,150/- is awarded towards loss of estate.
32. Medical Expenses:-
In the instant case, the petitioners have stated that, they have incurred Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, transportation, food and conveyance.

In order to substantiate the incurring of medical expenses, the petitioners have produced advance receipt bill marked at Ex.P16, medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P17 & medical bills marked at Ex.P18 amounting to Rs.53,847/-.
